episodes.212349: A moist and unstable weather pattern affected Puerto Rico from March 24 through March 28, 2026, as a mid- to upper-level trough interacted with abundant tropical moisture and favorable upper-level dynamics. Periods of heavy showers and thunderstorms developed across the island, resulting in flooding concerns, urban and small-stream flooding, and rapid rises on rivers and streams. The threat was enhanced by strong upper-level support associated with a strengthening jet stream and persistent moisture across the region.

events.narrative: Floodwaters from Rio Culebrinas impacted PR-110 KM 9.9 near Valle Encantado in sector Los Cocos. At the time, the USGS river sensor measured 22.4 ft.
Emergency managers reported flooding along PR-676 KM 1.6, near Mariposario Bosque la Vega in Vega Alta.
Emergency managers reported flooding along PR-2 near Ileana de Gracia high school.
Broadcast media shared on social media a report from floodwaters along PR-3 in direction to Tropical Beach in barrio Hucares in Naguabo.
Rio Yauco went out of its banks in barrio Barinas, near the treatment plant of Yauco in PR-335. The road was impassable.
Emergency management reported flooding along PR-31 in Naguabo due to the Rio Blanco overflowing its banks.
